t092: Install the Mac app. Open ingtype.dmg from the download link on this page and move the app to Applications. On first launch it asks for Accessibility permission: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility → turn on ingtype.
t093: Pair. Click the ingtype icon in the menu bar → Pair New Device. A 6-digit code appears.
t094: Open the app on your iPhone or iPad, choose your Mac and enter the code. After that it reconnects on its own.
t095: The Mac app is free. The download link goes up here on launch day (November). Your Mac and iPhone/iPad must be on the same Wi‑Fi.
t097: Lay the iPad flat and rest your wrists on the desk. iPadOS ignores touches near a resting wrist.
t098: In Settings → Multitasking & Gestures, turn off four/five-finger gestures so apps don't switch while you type.
t099: Modifier keys (shift, command…): tap once to apply to the next key, or hold while typing.
t100: Hold fn and tap the top row for F1–F12.
t101: For English-only legends: Settings → Keyboard → Key Legends → English Only.
t121: The air mouse covers long moves; the trackpad handles fine control. Adjust sensitivity in Settings. The iPhone keyboard mode can send emoji too.
t124: Make sure both devices are on the same Wi‑Fi. Guest, school and office networks often block device-to-device traffic.
t125: If so, turn on your iPhone's Personal Hotspot and join your Mac and iPad to it.
t126: Still missing? Connect by address: enter the address shown in the ingtype menu on your Mac (e.g. 172.20.10.2) under ‘Connect by Address…’.

t132: A code is valid for 2 minutes, and 5 wrong attempts require a new one. Close and reopen the pairing window on the Mac.
t134: The app is silent by default. Check that Key Click Sound is off in Settings.

t146: ingtype does not collect any personal information.
t149: create accounts, require sign-in, or collect identifiers such as email or phone number
t150: store or transmit the text you type, your keystrokes, or your pointer movements
t151: use advertising, analytics, or tracking SDKs
t152: talk to any external server (there is no developer server)
t154: ingtype only talks directly between your iPhone/iPad and your Mac on the same network.
t155: Traffic is encrypted with TLS. Only devices paired with the 6-digit code shown on the Mac can connect.
t156: Keystrokes are sent as key positions (key codes), not characters. They are handled as input the moment they reach the Mac and are never stored.
t157: When the iPhone keyboard sends a character with no key position, such as an emoji, the Mac briefly places it on the clipboard, pastes it, then restores your previous clipboard.
t158: If you choose ‘Mac Screen’ in the iPad mini window, only the one Mac window (or display) you picked is compressed into video and sent to that iPad over the same encrypted connection. It stops when you close the mini window or disconnect, and nothing is stored. The Mac menu bar shows it while sharing, with a way to stop at once. Handheld Mac works the same way: it shows your whole display, and only your taps and gestures go back to the Mac.
t159: Nothing is sent to the developer or third parties. Websites you open yourself in the mini window talk to those sites like any browser.
